Recommendation: refuse. Do not size this one.

Key reasons from the brief:
- Down 85% over 30 minutes and 90% off its 30-minute high. A coin in this state has an active sell-off, not a dip to buy.
- Last 15 minutes: sell SOL (9.41) is 73% of buy SOL (12.95), with net outflow in the window. Momentum is negative even though the +25% 15-minute return looks encouraging. Treat that bounce as noise against the larger collapse.
- Pool depth is only 30.56 SOL. A $20 ticket against that pool plus 1.4-5.1% round-trip costs and a 30-second execution lag means slippage and a stop that may not fill cleanly.
- Launch-bot presence and a 0.96 sell-to-buy ratio in the first two minutes point to early extraction. The 20% bundle share and 0.42 completer share are not reassuring either.
- Classification of ORGANIC does not offset these signals. The base rate for random buys in this regime is already negative.

If the desk overrode this refusal, the constraints would be: $5 ticket (the minimum), a 20% stop, and a 15-minute hold. But I would not recommend overriding. Refuse any size unless the 15-minute net flow turns clearly positive on rising buyer count and the pool depth grows meaningfully.
memos.scout:
The strongest honest case is thin. The curve shows real breadth: 898 buyers, a low top-3 share (7%), and a completer share of 42%, so the early buying wasn't concentrated in one wallet. The last 15 minutes are net positive (+3.54 SOL flow, +25% return, 53 buyers vs. 35 sellers), which is the only sign that buying pressure is still present.

But the brief undercuts that case. The coin is down 85% over 30 minutes and 90% from its 30-minute high, so the bounce is a dead-cat pattern, not a trend. Sell-to-buy in the first two minutes after graduation was 0.96, meaning early buyers were largely exiting into the launch. A launch bot was present, and the 190 SOL of early buying came from a crowd that has since been taking profit. The 25% recovery sits on a $2.6k volume base and a $6.2k market cap with a 30 SOL pool, so a $20 round trip at 1.4-5.1% costs little relative to the move, but the exit liquidity is shallow.

I don't see a case that real demand will persist 30-60 minutes out. The best that can be said is that the curve was broad and the last 15 minutes show a short-term bid. Against an ~20% base-rate loss for coins in this window and a clearly broken chart, I'd recommend skipping.
memos.skeptic: The most likely loss here is a continued dump after a 90% drawdown from the 30-minute high, with the buy side already exhausted. The last 15 minutes show sell SOL (9.41) against buy SOL (12.95), net flow still positive but the price is up 25% off a crash, so it looks like a bounce into sellers, not new demand. The first two minutes after graduation had a sell-to-buy ratio of 0.96 and a launch bot present, suggesting early buyers are already rotating out. Round-trip fees of 1.4-5.1% on a 30 SOL pool would eat any small bounce. Skip.
